name: Village Farms International, Inc.
hq: Lake Mary, Florida, USA (principal executive office per SEC filings; Canadian cannabis operations in Delta, British Columbia)
segment: Canadian LP / international greenhouse cannabis producer
headline_status: Village Farms is a former greenhouse produce grower that is now mainly a cannabis company, with a large EU-GMP greenhouse campus in British Columbia, a Dutch license and fast-growing exports to Europe.
summary: Village Farms spent decades growing greenhouse tomatoes before shifting to cannabis; it took its legacy produce business private in 2025 and now gets most of its revenue from cannabis. Its Pure Sunfarms business in Delta, British Columbia, runs what the company calls the world's largest EU-GMP certified cannabis facility, selling brands such as Pure Sunfarms, Fraser Valley Weed Co. and Soar in Canada and exporting medical cannabis, especially to Germany. It is also one of ten licensed growers in the Netherlands' regulated adult-use pilot, where a second Groningen facility began cultivation in 2026, and it owns CBDistillery in the U.S. along with stakes in cannabis businesses in Australia and Germany. In the quarter to June 30, 2026, sales rose 7% to $64.0 million, cannabis sales hit a record $53.5 million and exports grew 74%; net income was $7.1 million. The company raised $15 million from U.S. institutions in June 2026 and is due to report third-quarter results on November 9, 2026.

faq.q: Is Village Farms still a tomato grower?
faq.a: No longer as a public company business. It took its legacy produce operations private in 2025 and is now focused on cannabis, plus CBD and a clean-energy royalty business.

faq.q: Where does Village Farms grow cannabis?
faq.a: Mainly in greenhouses in Delta, British Columbia, and in the Netherlands, where it is one of ten licensed growers in the country's regulated cannabis program.

faq.q: Does Village Farms sell cannabis in the United States?
faq.a: Not THC cannabis. In the U.S. it sells CBD products through CBDistillery. The company says it is positioned to enter the U.S. market when regulations allow.
